mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.5% month-over-month signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the triggered instances, or the correlation between CPIAUCSL increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.2% month-over-month signals a tightening labor market, which is associated with increased economic activity and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the triggered instances, or the correlation between UNRATE decreases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over two consecutive months signals increased demand in the housing sector, which is a leading indicator of broader economic growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances following sustained increases in HOUST, or the correlation between HOUST increases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 4.5%, it signals a restrictive monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the triggered instances, or the correlation between high FEDFUNDS and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 jobs month-over-month, coupled with a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.2%, signals strong labor market conditions and is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the triggered instances, or the joint effect of PAYEMS and UNRATE changes on returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 0.5% month-over-month signals a contraction in the supply side of the economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the triggered instances, or the correlation between INDPRO decreases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over two consecutive months signals increased consumer demand, which is a leading indicator of economic growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances following sustained increases in RSAFS, or the correlation between RSAFS increases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1%, it signals an accommodative monetary policy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, especially in a low-interest-rate environment.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the triggered instances, or the correlation between low FEDFUNDS and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
